about: Every message Aaron typed or dictated in this session on Terra (the PC), copied verbatim from its log on 25 September 2026. Only his words. Taken from both places the log keeps them - the queued record of every message he sends and the plain user records - each message kept once at its earliest time. Messages he sent while Claude was still working sit in time order with the rest and are not marked apart, because a queued record alone does not show that. System text, tool output, skill instructions, task notifications, cross-session messages, compaction summaries and anything the studio wrote are excluded, as are the helper agents' logs beside this one.
title: Round 2 conquest ideation

messages.text: Read docs/design/DESIGNER-BRIEF.md and follow it — you are my game designer and co-ideation partner, stage 1 and 2 only. Round 2 (military conquest) is open, not closed: sixteen rulings and the whole relationship spine are settled, and docs/design/conquest-ideation.md §8 has the remaining questions in the order to ask them. Start with the Control Board card about whether a grudge fades on time or only when its cause goes away — that is also the first thing the round's closing trace has to run. Work down §8 one question at a time, then close the round by tracing the six scenarios in its §7 end to end, the way round 1 closed.

I think that grudge should fade over time. Maybe there is another state - weary - inbetween hostile and peace - so you can still trade with them and interact and they will make a trade with you but are weary and cautious. I think though having a trade deal and other things could increase how fast that state changes. but like you said if there is a growing movement or something else that would slow down how fast they get to peace.

I also think that all five texas states start hostile and they will all stay feeling that way at a minimum. Same with California, and the other city states trying to reunify the USA. That way it creates impositions and challenges. I think Austin would be wiped out pretty quickly because they have no trade possibility then, but that is ok with me
Resume
Here is my thought - if you have an ongoing trade deal it stays in place until the end of the trade deal but no new ones can be signed with them.

One other thought that I had for Austin specifically is that in the story Texas fell apart so we will say that because they were going to seceed from the union peacefully Austin is recognized as the actual state of texas by all other nations where as the El Paso, Dallas, Houston, and San Antonio are all seen as seccesionist movements. That would give Austin a bonus while the others have negatives.

Tolls dont have trade deal term lengths right? They are just set tolls? I still think that it should stay the same though.

Cease-fire can only result from a war. Hostile should only be resolved over time but I think there could be a diplomatic option (discussed later) where they would be basiclly improving relations and it would speed things up.

I would say that it would be the one sending the deal. So Utah invades Idaho. Idaho ends up winning. They send a deal to Utah some of their counties but because the war cost them money Utah has to pay them 1.25 the cost of the war so far.  (or maybe Utah comes back and says they will pay .5 the cost of their war and give the counties and idaho accepts

I think that the cost of war will be something that we need to create when we get to the economy section of war. My thought is that if Idaho is attacked they would lose income from those counties. And maybe that is another thing. If a county is attacked - even if not conquered it doesn't produce any income that turn.
One area per attack and I want to remove the 3 per turn and cooling down period. If a nation has the money and man power they can attack and organize as big of an attack as they want'
Lets go with your recomendation

It does eventually become your country and there will be certain modifiers that would either make it slow down or speed up.

So a county that was conquered by a nation that has a higher quality of life than the one it originally was in would be more willing to accept that they are apart of a new state.
Correct. If you are allied you share soldiers - but that should be a lever that you set and if you also border the country you could attack and invade as well.

Breaking a peace treaty lessens your relations to all of the nations around you. Lets say that unless you are allied to a country, any country that you border immeditaly turns hostile. (becuase if they are willing to break a peace treaty might we be next?)
Yes - because there is no treaty -they are just at peace.
Agree with your recomdation

Bases as a map feature:

* Army base (bonus to manpower)
* Air Force Base (bonus to attack)
* Naval Base (Bonus to coastal attacks and bonus to world/mexico/canada trade through ports)


No nuclear weapons

And lets pull in the data for military bases that won't get me put on a watch list
Sounds good

ignore politics I am working on it

/signoff
